explicit_definitions_given: categorical imperative as unconditional and universal
highest good as virtue and happiness proportioned

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Explicitly addresses the objection that postulates reintroduce heteronomy; refutes by distinguishing ground from condition and incentive from rational faith.
objections_raised: Postulates seem to make morality dependent on external reward
Belief in God might be motivated by self-interest

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, transcendental argument, thought experiments
named_thought_experiments: honest merchant vs. philanthropist acting from inclination

summary_of_core_decisions: The text presents a Kantian critique of eudaimonism, establishes the categorical imperative as the ground of morality, identifies an antinomy between virtue and happiness, and resolves it through the postulates of God and immortality while preserving autonomy.
